### B1 — The first second: a rectangle, never a spinner

The reader presses **Build the map**. Three things happen before any model call has returned.

1. The request goes. `generate()` posts and starts reading.
2. `generation_started` comes back at once — the engine emits it before its first call, so it costs
   nothing to wait for — carrying the generation's identifier, the seed, the sentence as typed, and
   the destination if there was one.
3. **One skeleton tile is drawn**, in the leftmost column, carrying the reader's own sentence.

That third step is the first paint, and it is on screen in the time one round trip to our own server
takes. It carries no likelihood, because nothing has computed one; it carries the reader's words,
because the reader typed them.

**What that first rectangle is standing in for.** One call — the one that turns the typed sentence
into a checkable claim. It arrives as an ordinary `proposal_accepted` at `at: 0` with an **empty**
`links`, because the hypothesis has nothing before it, and the rectangle becomes H's tile. On the
Verify door a second such call follows at `at: 1` for the destination, and it too is an ordinary
claim with no arrows in. There is no separate event for either, and the browser needs none: from this
side both are the same fact the rest of the run keeps repeating — *the map got bigger*.

**NFR-7's wording is corrected here.** It reads *"streaming first-paint within 1s of the first
token"*, and this pipeline has no first token to be within a second of: the model boundary returns
**one whole proposal per call** (record 0006), and one proposal takes seconds to come back. A budget
measured from the first token would be a budget nothing could ever miss, because the thing it starts
timing from arrives at the same moment as the thing it times. So the budget is measured from the
request being accepted, and what has to be on screen within the second is a skeleton at its column —
which is the honest reading of what UX-8 promises anyway. **NFR-7 now reads that way**, amended
2026-09-20 in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` itself, so the two no longer disagree.

**There is no spinner anywhere in this product** — not here, not on the launchpad, not on the
`insert` route, not while a lazily fetched midpoint chip is in flight. Waiting is always shown as the
shape of the thing being waited for: a reserved rectangle where a claim will go, an absence with its
reason where a number will go. Checklist `VR2` is the standing check and
`test_there_is_no_spinner_anywhere` is the automated one.

### B2 — What a skeleton is, and what it never becomes

A skeleton tile is **a reserved rectangle**. Not a shimmer, not a pulse, not a grey bar sliding
across a card.

content.content:
## ANTI-PATTERNS

1. **Do not put a spinner anywhere, not even for a moment, not even a small one.** *Because* a
   spinner says only "wait", and the thing being waited for has a shape — a claim at a column, a
   number in a slot — which says "wait" *and* what for *and* where it will land. It is also a named
   veto condition (PRD §10 anti-pattern 9). **Instead:** a reserved rectangle where the claim goes,
   and an absence with its reason where the number goes.

2. **Do not animate a skeleton.** *Because* a shimmer is a tool performing busyness at a reader who
   is waiting on a model call that takes seconds, and the fourth animation would be the one that
   turns a motion budget into a suggestion. **Instead:** a still rectangle, appearing and going with
   an opacity change of at most 120 milliseconds.

3. **Do not let a belief chip fill in as its causes arrive.** *Because* a likelihood computed from
   half a map is the answer to a question about a map that will not exist in a second, and a number
   that changes four times is four numbers nobody computed. **Instead:** every chip reads *no engine
   yet* until `beliefs_propagated`, and then they all resolve at once, once.

4. **Do not hide, merge or summarise a refusal.** *Because* watching our own rules turn the model
   down is the evidence that the model is not in charge of the map, and a run that shows only its
   successes is a demo rather than a tool. **Instead:** one row per refusal, every sentence the
   validator wrote, kept on screen for the run and in the transcript afterwards.

5. **Do not draw a refused claim as a faint tile, a ghost or a struck-through box.** *Because* the
   moment it has a box it needs an identifier, and the model would then have caused an identifier to
   exist — which the schema is shaped to make impossible. **Instead:** quote its words in the strip
   and give it nothing else.

   fabrication in the exact place the honesty bar exists to prevent one (FR-7). **Instead:** the

   failure the whole layout chapter exists to prevent. **Instead:** pin absolutely, let a late arrival
   find a gap, and say out loud what that costs (B3).

   a percentage nobody computed is a number nobody computed wearing a progress bar, and the caps that
   would have to be divided by are the server's and are not on the stream. **Instead:** show what has

    differ by half a point nobody can say which is right. **Instead:** the drawing is thrown away
    when `beliefs_propagated` arrives, and the engine's world is the world.

    number in the request that nobody elicited, and it would sit on the hypothesis as a `user` belief
    for the rest of the session. **Instead:** send no user belief at all, and let the slot read its
    own absence.

    already standing there or is about to belong to this one at coordinates the layout chose — so the
    box lands where it does not belong and then moves, on the one screen whose whole promise is that
    nothing already drawn moves. **Instead:** draw nothing that has no place, and let the rectangle
    already standing go on saying where the claim is going until the claim itself is drawn.

## Open questions

*Raised 2026-09-17.*

1. **Should the stream say when a call goes out?** The eight events say what came back, so the
   browser can draw the frontier but cannot honestly say how many proposals are in flight — three
   calls against one open claim show one rectangle (B2). A ninth event would fix it and would also be
   the first event that carries no decision, only activity, which is a different kind of thing to put
   on a stream. **Owner:** `spec/generation/streaming.md`, if anyone ever wants the count on screen.

2. **Does the map re-lay out once when the run finishes?** **Answered 2026-09-21: no — and the real
   question turned out to be a different one.**

   The measurement, taken on the coordinator's ten-claim run at 1600 × 1000, the size the whole
   interface is designed against: the stage is **1264 × 801**, the map is framed at **0.85** — the
   floor below which a tile would have to become a summary — and at that framing **six of the ten
   tiles are whole on the glass, four are wholly below it and none is cut**. No arrow points
   backwards, on this run or on the chapter's own, so the thing a re-layout would have tidied did not
   happen; what did happen is that **a third of the map was off the screen with nothing saying so**,
   which is far worse and is not a layout problem at all. A map that is cut with nothing saying so is
   read as a map that ends there, and for a causal map that is the worst thing it can be read as: the
   reader concludes the argument stops where the window does.

   So the answer is the one that costs the reader nothing: **the map is never re-laid out, and the
   stage says where it is cut.** A two-pixel rule in `--text-muted` sits at whichever edge has map
   beyond it and at no edge that has not — the same rule, the same weight and the same colour the
   panel beside it already uses for the same fact, drawn as the four sides of one box so a corner
   reads as a corner. The stage measures it about itself, because the two boxes are measured
   differently: a panel is scrolled and a stage is panned.

   Re-laying out would still move every tile once at the moment the reader starts reading, and it
   would still not put the four tiles on the glass — there is no zoom that fits ten tiles in 1264 ×
   801 and keeps them readable, which is exactly why the zoom floor exists. **Owner:** closed.

3. **What does an `insert` cost, and where does that show?** **Answered 2026-09-20 by
   [`spec/generation/streaming.md`](../generation/streaming.md), drawn 2026-09-21, and nothing is
   open.** The route answers a `DraftedInsert` — the edit and its own `Receipt` — and the cost is
   drawn beside the drafted claim by the same strip, with the same ten readings, that a generation's
   receipt is drawn by. What made it answerable was learning that an insert is **several** calls
   rather than one: the starting-claim shape drafts the reader's sentence, and then the ordinary walk
   proposes its arrows, one call each. A running total in the browser lost on two counts — it is a
   number added up by something other than the engine, and it vanishes on a page reload. **Owner:**
   closed. See B8.

4. **Where does a replayed run's pacing come from, and is it the same on every machine?**
   **Answered 2026-09-17 by `spec/generation/replay.md`, and nothing is open.** The delay is fixed on
   the **server** — an argument with a default the builder picks against a measurement, because a
   replay that races teaches a reviewer that the product is faster than it is — so two readers' replays
   are the same length. It is **one setting**, `KATALYST_REPLAY_PACE` in seconds, read once by
   `katalyst.settings` and never a field on the request: a client that could ask for a replay with no
   pause would let anyone with the network tab open skip the thing the recording exists to show. A
   pace of zero means no pause at all, which is the same question answered with a smaller number
   rather than a second switch beside it *(2026-09-21; it was a length and an `instant` flag)*. **The browser
   therefore paces nothing, waits on nothing, and has no pacing code at all** — it reads events as
   they arrive, which is the same thing it does live.

5. **How long is a refusal strip allowed to get?** Three refusals close an open claim and the caps
   bound the whole run, so the strip is bounded — but nothing says by what, and a run that refused
   twenty proposals would fill the dock and push the Inspector off the screen. Scrolling the strip is
   the obvious answer and it is also the answer that lets a reader miss a refusal. **Owner:** this
   chapter, once a real run has been watched.

# A — the run says what it is doing, and the provenance footer steps back

Analyst UA, 2026-09-21. Read-only pass over `main` at `feda9ac`. Scripts: `plans/analysis/scripts/ux-round/A/`.

---

## 1. What is true today

**The foot of a generating map has three strips, and none of them is about the run.**
`components/MapFrame.tsx:116` draws *last key* (what the keyboard did). `MapFrame.tsx:138` draws the live region. `MapFrame.tsx:147` draws the provenance line.

**The one sentence about the run is invisible.** `GenerationScreen.tsx:304` passes `spokenOnly={true}`; `components/generationDock.css:38-48` clips `.map-live--spoken` to one pixel. So *"Asked for a map of … A rectangle is held open where the first claim will go"* (`a11y/growth.ts:42-47`) is spoken and never shown. `e2e/generate.spec.ts:230` **asserts** that hiding, which is why no test could ever have caught it.

**The provenance line asserts arrivals on an empty map.** `stream/growth.ts:192-200` writes *"Every claim and arrow on this map arrived from /api/generate…"* from `generation_started` onward — before one claim exists (`plans/logs/m4-look/02-one-second-after.png`).

**"Read the working of this run →" is offered from the first event and never resolves.** The control renders whenever `generationId !== null` (`GenerationScreen.tsx:346`), but the fetch is gated on `finished` (`GenerationScreen.tsx:96-99`), so pressing it mid-run leaves *"Reading the working of this run back from the server…"* (`components/Inspector.tsx:905-909`) until the run ends.

**How long the silences are.** Measured: `medium` effort, **51.98 s per call** (`plans/logs/eval-hormuz-medium.log`); the recorder's effort, **109.65 s per call** (`plans/logs/eval-hormuz.log`). A round asks three claims at once (`engine/outcome.py:311`, `at_once: 3`), so events land in bursts of up to three and then the screen is still for about a minute.

**What the server knows and does not say.** Nothing records that a call went out. `grow.py:243-256` submits a round to a thread pool and the next thing anyone sees is an answer. `following.py:109-115` folds only returned answers. So *which claim is open* is on the wire (`frontier`, on both growth events — `engine/events.py:114,143`) and *which three are in flight*, *whether a search is running*, *call number* and *tokens so far* are not on it at all. The receipt carries calls, tokens and searches and arrives second-to-last (`engine/events.py:166-217`).

**What the browser already holds** (measured off `backend/recordings/hormuz.jsonl` by `plans/analysis/scripts/ux-round/A/what_the_wire_already_says.py`): 26 events; the transcript counter `at` runs 0→22; claims 0→18; places held open 0→5; refusals 0→3. The receipt's 29 calls against 23 growth events is the gap — **the browser can honestly count proposals, never calls.**

**Polling the transcript adds nothing.** `transcript.py:60-120` gains a line only when a call *returns*; every returning call that changes the map already made an event. The only extra is a `stopped` line — the model saying a line is finished.

**Elsewhere.** The stored map already says something while `/api/worlds` runs (65–500 ms): `MapScreen.tsx:718` prints `WHILE_ASKING.reason`. The launchpad already says *"Asking the server whether this one can be run here…"* (`Launchpad.tsx:378`). **Both are right already; only the generating screen is silent.**

---

## 2. Three designs

### A1 — Recommended: one strip at the foot, and it says the sentence out loud *and* in ink

The foot of both map screens becomes **one** strip. Left, the state as one word in the mono box `.map-status__mark` already uses; then one human sentence; then, only while a run is open, `nothing new for 47 s`. The provenance line moves into a **Run details** section of the panel (this is R16, pulled forward from 06-4). `spokenOnly` is deleted — not guarded — because the duplication it was added to prevent is exactly what the provenance move removes.

```
┌ map ─────────────────────────────────────────────┬ panel ───────┐
│           ┌ HELD OPEN ─────────┐                 │ Run details ▸│
│           │ The Strait of      │                 │ Nothing      │
│           │ Hormuz …           │                 │ selected     │
│           └────────────────────┘                 │              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────┤
│ last key  Press ? for every key. j and k walk a column…         │
│ ┌live┐ One place is held open where the first claim will go.    │
│ └────┘                              nothing new for 23 s        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The sentence, in each state.** Every one of these strings exists today; the strip is where they land.

| State | Word | The one sentence |
|---|---|---|
| stored map | `stored` | `world.origin` — *this map was built earlier and is drawn as it was written* |
| stored map, engine asked | `asking` | `WHILE_ASKING.reason` (`MapScreen.tsx:70`) + `nothing new for 0.4 s` |
| replay | `replay` | `replaySentence(…)` + *four claims so far, three places held open* |
| live and waiting | `live` | `theOpeningLine` (`a11y/growth.ts:42`) + `nothing new for 23 s` |
| live and arriving | `live` | `whatChanged` (`a11y/growth.ts:58`) + `nothing new for 6 s` |
| finished | `finished` | `WHY_IT_STOPPED[reason]` (`DoneLine.tsx:23`) with the run's own counts |
| failed | `stopped` | the one plain sentence the run left |
| stopped early | `ended early` | `THE_STREAM_ENDED_EARLY` (`DoneLine.tsx:53`) + how many claims arrived first |

**Code:** one component (~90 lines) + one CSS block; `MapFrame.tsx` loses the `spokenOnly` prop and gains the strip; `GenerationScreen.tsx` and `MapScreen.tsx` each lose their `origin` block; `Inspector.tsx` gains *Run details*; `generationDock.css:38-48` deleted; one line in `GenerationScreen.tsx:346` gates the working control on `finished`. **Cost:** ~1.5 sessions. **Risk:** small — the elapsed reading must sit outside the announced region or a screen reader speaks every second (below).

**Why this one.** One rule instead of three: *the foot says one sentence about the run, and it is the same sentence the live region speaks.* It removes a special case rather than adding a channel, it needs no server change, and it is the only candidate where the answer to "is anything happening?" and the answer to "what did it just do?" cannot drift apart.

### A2 — A ninth event, `asking`

Before each round the server names the claims it is about to ask about and whether the call may search; those rectangles read `ASKING` instead of `HELD OPEN`. **Code:** `events.py` (+1 shape, +1 name), `grow.py` widens its yield type, `following.py` passes it through without billing it, `replay.py` decides what a recording without it means, the grammar tests, then `events.ts` + the reducer + the rectangle. ~2 sessions. **Cost it carries:** the four recordings do not hold it, so a replay would be visibly less alive than a live run — and *the same events, the same framing, the same canvas* is the sentence record 0012 rests on (`api/generate.py:16-23`). It would have to ride the one shape freeze (R9, 05-5) so all four recordings carry it. Not now; A1 does not block it.

### A3 — Poll the transcript while the run is open

Free — the route already answers in flight (`api/generate.py:463`). **Measured above: it tells the browser nothing the stream has not already told it**, except that the model closed a line. Two copies of one state for one fact. Not recommended.

---

## 3. The rule about motion, written so a test can hold it

> **Motion may carry information; it may never stand in for it.** A thing on screen may change over time only when what changes is a **measurement** — a value the screen would print anyway — and the sentence beside it is complete without the change. Nothing loops, spins, pulses or sweeps: a repeat is motion with no measurement behind it. Under reduced motion the measurement still updates, because it is information and not a tween.

**`motionBudget.test.ts` needs no change at all.** The elapsed reading is a number redrawn by a timer in JavaScript; it spends no CSS duration, so the three tokens and the reduced-motion assertions stand exactly as written. **`noSpinner.test.ts` keeps its three lines untouched** — nothing rotates, nothing is an indeterminate progress indicator, nothing is called a loader — and gains one: `test_the_only_thing_that_changes_on_a_timer_is_a_measured_reading`, a walk for `setInterval`/`setTimeout` in product code against a named allowlist, the technique `colourLaw.test.ts` already uses. That is the whole line between Kent's veto and Kent's ask.

**Accessibility.** The sentence stays in the `aria-live="polite"` region and keeps saying what *changed* (INV-workbench.78). The elapsed reading sits beside it, not inside it and not `aria-hidden` — plain text, navigable, never announced. A counter inside the region would speak every second.

---

## 4. Earlier decisions this touches, with the amendment

| Decision | Amendment (dated `2026-09-21`) |
|---|---|
| **New record, `proposed`** — next free number after 0016–0022 land | *"Motion may carry information; it may never stand in for it. A thing on screen may change over time only when what changes is a measurement, and the sentence beside it is complete without that change. Nothing loops, spins, pulses or sweeps. The disgust veto's 'spinner followed by a dump of results' is unchanged: what it forbids is motion in place of a sentence, not a number that changes because time passed."* |
| **PRD UX-8** *(streaming is the loading state; no spinner)* | add: *"…and the screen says, in words, what it is waiting for and how long it has been waiting. Silence is not a loading state."* |
| **PRD §10 anti-pattern 9** | add the clause: *"…a spinner-then-dump — motion standing in for a sentence. A measurement that changes is not one."* |
| **INV-workbench.78** *(the live region says what changed)* | *"…and the same sentence is printed at the foot of the screen. There is no state in which the only account of what the run is doing is spoken."* Deletes `spokenOnly`. |
| **`streaming-growth.md` anti-pattern 8** *(no estimate of cost, progress or remaining claims)* | add: *"How long it has been since the last event is a measurement, not an estimate, and is allowed. How much longer it will take is an estimate, and is not."* |
| **`streaming-growth.md` open question 1** *(should the stream say when a call goes out?)* | Answered: *"Not in version one. Everything the foot strip says is already on the eight events or on the browser's own clock. A ninth event would be the first to carry activity rather than a decision, and no committed recording holds it — so if it is ever wanted it rides the one shape freeze, where all four recordings are made together."* |
| **R16** *(Run details moves into the panel; the strip keeps one human sentence)* | Pulled forward from 06-4 to this stack. It is what makes un-hiding the sentence safe — nothing else at the foot then repeats it. No new record; R16 already says this. |
| **Record 0008** *(three tiers of browser testing)* | No amendment. This is timing-sensitive code → tier 2 → a no-browser test that injects the adverse timing. Built below. |
| **INV-workbench.60, .18, .73; `noSpinner`; `motionBudget`** | **Unchanged.** Named here so the record says what it did *not* move. |

---

## 5. What waits on Kent — three questions

1. **Is a number that ticks the motion you meant?** *Hormuz:* while the model works on the next three claims, the foot reads `live · One place is held open where the first claim will go. nothing new for 23 s`, and the seconds count up. Nothing spins, nothing pulses. **Recommended: yes** — it is motion that carries a measurement, so it survives the veto that "a spinner followed by a dump of results" names. If you want a visible non-textual mark as well, say so and it becomes a fourth design question, because every honest one needs a number the server does not send.
2. **Pull R16 forward into this stack?** *Hormuz:* the sentence naming `/api/generate`, generation `01M32NFP…` and seed `8945432650305861` leaves the foot and becomes a *Run details* section of the panel; the foot carries the run's one sentence instead. **Recommended: yes** — R16 already decided the move; this only changes when. It is also what makes the hidden sentence safe to show.
3. **The ninth event — hold it for the freeze, or drop it for good?** *Hormuz:* with it, the three rectangles being worked on read `ASKING` and the rest read `HELD OPEN`. **Recommended: hold, and decide at the freeze** — no committed recording carries it, so building it now makes a replay visibly less alive than a live run.

---

## 6. The work, as two pull requests

**`docs/07-one-sentence-about-the-run`** → `main`. The new record `proposed`; the seven amendments above; `spec/workbench/streaming-growth.md` B1 and B10 rewritten for the strip; open question 1 closed; `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s browser section. **0.5 session.**

**`feat/07-the-run-strip`** → the docs branch. The strip; `spokenOnly` deleted; provenance into *Run details*; the working control gated on `finished`; the elapsed clock. **1.5 sessions.** Tested by:

- **`frontend/src/stream/__tests__/theRunStrip.test.tsx` — the test that would have caught what Kent saw.** No browser, fake timers: fold `generation_started`, advance 23 s, assert the *visible* strip names what is held open and reads `nothing new for 23 s`. Then fold a `proposal_accepted` and assert it resets. This is R33's tier 2 twin, and it is the only kind of test that can see a live wait, because `playwright.config.ts:158` gives every browser test an empty key and `:209` paces every replay at 0.4 s.
- **`e2e/generate.spec.ts`**: line 230's `toHaveClass(/map-live--spoken/)` is **deleted and inverted** — at the one 0.4 s gap the suite already brackets, the strip must be visible and must name what is being waited for. Its `howOften === 1` check survives, because `DoneLine` becomes the strip's finished face rather than a second copy.
- **`noSpinner.test.ts`** gains `test_the_only_thing_that_changes_on_a_timer_is_a_measured_reading`.
- Sweep: `map-live--spoken` and `map-origin` appear in `generationDock.css`, `app.css:415-433`, both screens and two specs.

Order: docs first (Kent reads the record), code on it. Two deep, per R13. **Nothing here is blocked by stack 05 or 06**, and nothing in it touches the prompt, so R5's freeze is untouched.

---

## 7. What I would not do

1. **A progress bar, a percentage, or "about a minute left."** The caps that would have to be divided by are the server's and are not on the wire (`streaming-growth.md` anti-pattern 8). 51.98 s a call is a measurement of *another* run, not of this one.
2. **Any looping motion** — a pulsing rectangle, a breathing dot, a shimmer. `noSpinner.test.ts` forbids it, and it is the fourth animation that turns a budget into a suggestion.
3. **A ninth event this week.** §2 A2.
4. **Polling the transcript mid-run.** Measured: nothing new, and a second copy of one state.
5. **Making the replay faster so the wait feels shorter.** A replay that races teaches a reviewer the product is faster than it is (`replay.md`, open question 4).
6. **Saying "3 calls in flight".** The browser cannot know `at_once`; `/api/about` publishes no caps. It can count proposals, and it should say *proposals*.

---

## Five-line summary

1. **The mechanism:** the one sentence about a live run exists and is clipped to one pixel (`generationDock.css:38`, `GenerationScreen.tsx:304`), a browser test asserts that clipping (`generate.spec.ts:230`), and the foot instead carries a provenance line claiming arrivals on an empty map (`growth.ts:192`) — while a call takes 52 s at `medium` and 110 s at the recorder's effort.
2. **Recommended:** one strip at the foot of both map screens, printing the sentence the live region already speaks plus `nothing new for N s`; provenance moves into *Run details* (R16, pulled forward from 06-4), which is what makes the un-hiding safe. No server change; ~2 sessions across two pull requests.
3. **The motion line, testable:** *motion may carry information, never stand in for it* — `motionBudget` and `noSpinner` are unchanged, and `noSpinner` gains one allowlist check over timers, so a ticking measurement is legal and a pulse still is not.
4. **The gap in the tests:** every browser test runs with an empty key and a 0.4 s replay pace, so no test can see a live wait; a no-browser twin with fake timers is the one that would have caught this, and it is tier 2 of record 0008.
5. **Waiting on Kent:** is a ticking number the motion he meant; may R16 come forward now; and is the ninth event (`asking`) held for the one shape freeze or dropped — recommendations are yes, yes, hold.

1. **A progress bar, a percentage, or "about a minute left."** The caps that would have to be divided by are the server's and are not on the wire (`streaming-growth.md` anti-pattern 8). 51.98 s a call is a measurement of *another* run, not of this one.

**Code:** one component (~90 lines) + one CSS block; `MapFrame.tsx` loses the `spokenOnly` prop and gains the strip; `GenerationScreen.tsx` and `MapScreen.tsx` each lose their `origin` block; `Inspector.tsx` gains *Run details*; `generationDock.css:38-48` deleted; one line in `GenerationScreen.tsx:346` gates the working control on `finished`. **Cost:** ~1.5 sessions. **Risk:** small — the elapsed reading must sit outside the announced region or a screen reader speaks every second (below).

Plan written to `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/ux-round/A-live-status.md` (~2 580 words — over the 1 500 bar, because the brief asked for the seven-state table, the motion rule, and two amendment tables on top of the common six sections). Evidence script at `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/ux-round/A/what_the_wire_already_says.py`. The repository is otherwise untouched (`git status` clean; `plans/` is git-ignored).

## Five-line summary

1. **The mechanism:** the one sentence about a live run exists and is clipped to one pixel (`frontend/src/components/generationDock.css:38`, `frontend/src/stream/GenerationScreen.tsx:304`), a browser test *asserts* that clipping (`frontend/e2e/generate.spec.ts:230`), and the foot instead carries a provenance line claiming arrivals on an empty map (`frontend/src/stream/growth.ts:192`) — while a call takes 51.98 s at `medium` and 109.65 s at the recorder's effort (`plans/logs/eval-hormuz-medium.log`, `plans/logs/eval-hormuz.log`).
2. **Recommended:** one strip at the foot of both map screens, printing the sentence the live region already speaks plus `nothing new for N s`; provenance moves into *Run details* (R16, pulled forward from 06-4), which is what makes the un-hiding safe. No server change; ~2 sessions across two pull requests.
3. **The motion line, testable:** *motion may carry information, never stand in for it* — `motionBudget` and `noSpinner` are unchanged, and `noSpinner` gains one allowlist check over timers, so a ticking measurement is legal and a pulse still is not.
4. **The gap in the tests:** every browser test runs with an empty key and a 0.4 s replay pace (`frontend/playwright.config.ts:158,209`), so no test can see a live wait; a no-browser twin with fake timers is the one that would have caught this, and it is tier 2 of record 0008.
5. **Waiting on Kent:** is a ticking number the motion he meant; may R16 come forward now; is the ninth event (`asking`) held for the one shape freeze or dropped — recommendations are yes, yes, hold.

## Questions that wait on Kent

1. **Is a number that ticks the motion you meant?** While the model works on the next three Hormuz claims the foot reads `live · One place is held open where the first claim will go. nothing new for 23 s`, seconds counting up; nothing spins or pulses. Recommended: yes. A visible non-textual mark as well is a separate question, because every honest version of one needs a number the server does not send.
2. **Pull R16 forward into this stack?** The sentence naming `/api/generate`, generation `01M32NFP…` and seed `8945432650305861` leaves the foot for a *Run details* section of the panel. Recommended: yes — R16 already decided the move; this changes only when, and it is what makes showing the hidden sentence safe.
3. **The ninth event (`asking`) — hold it for the one shape freeze, or drop it?** With it, the three rectangles in flight would read `ASKING` and the rest `HELD OPEN`. Recommended: hold and decide at the freeze — no committed recording carries it, so building it now would make a replay visibly less alive than a live run, breaking the promise record 0012 rests on.

Two findings worth flagging beyond the brief: **"Read the working of this run →" is offered from the first event but its fetch is gated on the run finishing** (`GenerationScreen.tsx:96-99` vs `:346`), so pressing it mid-run shows *"Reading the working…"* forever — a one-line fix. And **polling the transcript mid-run would add nothing**: `transcript.py:60-120` gains a line only when a call returns, and every returning call that changes the map already makes an event.
